title: Small Horde
capsule: The Small (Lesser) Nogai Horde split off from the main Nogai Horde around 1557–1564, when the mirza Kazy broke with the Volga-based leadership and led his followers to the Kuban steppe east of the Sea of Azov. Settling as a nominal vassal of the Crimean Khanate, the Lesser Horde fractured further, and it and related Nogai groups such as the Budjak, Yedisan, and Kuban hordes raided and traded along the corridor linking the lower Volga to the Black Sea. Weakened by Kalmyk invasions in the 17th century and growing Russian power, the horde was progressively absorbed into the Russian and Crimean spheres through the early 18th century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Nogai territorial extents are derived from Russian and Ottoman diplomatic records and traveler accounts describing general zones of migration and tribute; as a nomadic confederation, precise boundaries cannot be established, and the mapped extent is a best estimate of seasonal range rather than a controlled territory. Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: medium).
